title: Chevalley: a scheme receiving a finite surjective morphism from an affine scheme is affine
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume that $f$ is finite [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism] and surjective, i.e. $|X|\to|S|$ is surjective [def-weil-surjective-morphism], and that $X$ is an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Then $S$ is an affine scheme.

source.place: Limits, Lemma 01ZT (label lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), with its proof (S quasi-compact and separated by Morphisms 01WM and 09MQ; reduction to f finite of finite presentation by Limits lemma-finite-in-finite-and-finite-presentation and 01Z6; absolute Noetherian approximation, Limits proposition-approximate, descent of finite morphisms of finite presentation; Noetherian case Cohomology of Schemes lemma-image-affine-finite-morphism-affine-Noetherian)

proof.text: ($S$ is quasi-compact, separated and quasi-separated.) Let $p:X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ and $q:S\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ be the structure morphisms; $q\circ f=p$ since a morphism into $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is a ring map $\mathbf Z\to\Gamma$, which is unique [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme]. Since $X$ is affine, $p$ is a morphism between affine schemes, hence affine, hence quasi-compact and separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3); so $X$ is quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] and $|S|=f(|X|)$ [def-weil-surjective-morphism] is quasi-compact as a continuous image of a quasi-compact space. The finite $f$ is integral [lem-weil-pbc-finite-iff-integral-lft], hence universally closed [pqf-lem-integral-univclosed] (Morphisms 01WM). As $f$ is surjective and universally closed and $p$ is separated, $q$ is separated [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-universally-closed-separated] (Morphisms 09MQ). Then the diagonal $S\to S\times_{\mathbf Z}S$ is a closed immersion, hence affine [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-integral-separated-uc] (b), hence quasi-compact [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3): $S$ is quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions].

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma 01ZT (lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), first paragraph (Morphisms 01WM, 09MQ); the quasi-separatedness of S, needed for 09YZ and 01ZA, is written out by the agent

proof.text:
(Reduction to $f$ of finite presentation.) $f$ is integral (step 1) and $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, so by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-morphism-limit-of-finite] (Limits 09YZ) there are a directed set $A$, $S$-schemes $
u_a:X_a	o S$ that are finite and of finite presentation [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], affine transition morphisms over $S$ and morphisms $p_a:X	o X_a$ over $S$ (so $f=
u_a\circ p_a$) with $X=\varprojlim_aX_a$. Each $
u_a$ is affine, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (3), so every $X_a$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2); as the limit $X$ is affine, some $X_{a_0}$ is affine [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-stage] (Limits 01Z6). $
u_{a_0}$ is surjective because $f=
u_{a_0}\circ p_{a_0}$ is [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Replacing $(X,f)$ by $(X_{a_0},
u_{a_0})$ we may and do assume from now on that $f$ is finite, of finite presentation and surjective and $X$ is affine (step 1 still applies).

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma 01ZT (lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), second paragraph (Stacks cites Lemma 09YY lemma-finite-in-finite-and-finite-presentation, whose transition maps are closed immersions; the agent uses the existing node for its generalization 09YZ to integral f, whose affine transitions are all that Lemma 01Z6 needs; the qcqs hypotheses of 01Z6 are checked by the agent)

proof.text: (Absolute Noetherian approximation of $S$.) $S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (step 1), so by [prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system] (Limits 01ZA; Lean closed) it has a Noetherian approximation [def-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system]: a cofiltered diagram of schemes of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with affine transition morphisms and a limit cone with vertex $S$. By [lem-weil-pbc-cofiltered-limit-directed-reindex] it is reindexed by a nonempty directed set $I$: an inverse system $(S_i,f_{ii'})_{i\in I}$ of schemes of finite type over $\mathbf Z$ with affine transitions and $S=\varprojlim_iS_i$, projections $\sigma_i:S\to S_i$. Every $S_i$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact, hence also quasi-separated [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated].

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma 01ZT (lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), third paragraph, first sentence (Proposition 01ZA proposition-approximate)

proof.text: (Descending $f$ to a finitely presented model.) $f$ is of finite presentation and the $S_i$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated with affine transitions, so by [thm-pd-spreading-out] (1) (Limits 01ZM) there are $0\in I$, a morphism of finite presentation $g_0:X_0\to S_0$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] and an isomorphism $X\cong X_0\times_{S_0}S$ over $S$ (fibre product along $\sigma_0$ [def-pc-fibre-product]). The subset $I_{\ge0}$ is cofinal, so $S=\varprojlim_{i\ge0}S_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory]; we index by $I_{\ge0}$ from now on. Put $X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i$ and $g_i:X_i\to S_i$ the projection. By [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-over-limit] (Limits 01YZ) $(X_i)_{i\ge0}$ is an inverse system with affine transition morphisms whose limit is $X_0\times_{S_0}S\cong X$. Each $g_i$ is of finite presentation as a base change of $g_0$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (3), so $X_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated over the quasi-compact quasi-separated $S_i$ [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence] (2). In the notation of the descent lemmas (Situation 081D) with $Y_0=S_0$ and $f_0=g_0$: $Y_i=S_0\times_{S_0}S_i=S_i$, $f_i=g_i$, and the base change of $f_0$ to $S$ is $X_0\times_{S_0}S\to S$, which is $f$ up to the isomorphism over $S$.

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma 01ZT (lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), third paragraph, second sentence (Lemma 01ZM lemma-descend-finite-presentation; Stacks' 'X_{i'} = X_i x_S S_{i'}' is a misprint for X_i x_{S_i} S_{i'}); the qcqs hypotheses and cofinality are written out by the agent

proof.text: ($g_i$ is finite for large $i$.) $f$ is finite and $g_0$ is locally of finite type, being locally of finite presentation (a finitely presented algebra is finitely generated) [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]; $S_0$, $X_0$ are quasi-compact and quasi-separated (steps 3, 4). By [lem-weil-pbc-descend-finite] (Limits 01ZO) $g_{i_1}$ is finite for some $i_1\ge0$. For $i\ge i_1$, $X_i=X_0\times_{S_0}S_i\cong X_{i_1}\times_{S_{i_1}}S_i$ by pasting fibre squares [def-pc-fibre-product], so $g_i$ is a base change of $g_{i_1}$ and is finite [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] (a).

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma 01ZT (lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), third paragraph, third sentence (Lemma 01ZO lemma-descend-finite-finite-presentation); stability under increasing i written out by the agent

proof.text: ($g_i$ is surjective for large $i$.) $f$ is surjective and $g_0$ is locally of finite presentation, so by [lem-weil-pbc-descend-surjective] (Limits 07RR) $g_{i_2}$ is surjective for some $i_2\ge0$; for $i\ge i_2$, $g_i$ is a base change of $g_{i_2}$ (as in step 5) and is surjective [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change].

source.place: Not in Stacks' proof of 01ZT, which applies the Noetherian case to X_i -> S_i without saying why it is surjective; the agent supplies Limits Lemma 07RR (lemma-descend-surjective, limits.tex line 2069)

proof.text: ($X_i$ is affine for large $i$.) $(X_i)_{i\ge0}$ is a directed inverse system of quasi-compact quasi-separated schemes with affine transitions whose limit is isomorphic to the affine $X$ (step 4), hence affine [def-pc-scheme]; by [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-stage] (Limits 01Z6) there is $i_3$ with $X_i$ affine for all $i\ge i_3$.

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma 01ZT (lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), third paragraph, fourth sentence ('By Lemma 01Z6 once again we may assume that X_i is affine for all i')

proof.text: (The Noetherian case.) Choose $i\in I$ with $i\ge i_1,i_2,i_3$ ($I$ directed). Then $g_i:X_i\to S_i$ is finite (step 5) and surjective (step 6), $X_i$ is affine (step 7) and $S_i$ is Noetherian (step 3). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-surjective-affine-target-noetherian] (Cohomology of Schemes 01YQ) $S_i$ is affine.

source.place: Limits, proof of Lemma 01ZT (lemma-affine, limits.tex line 2834), last sentence (Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YQ lemma-image-affine-finite-morphism-affine-Noetherian)

proof.text: (Conclusion.) The projection $\sigma_i:S\to S_i$ of the limit of an inverse system with affine transitions is affine [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], and $S_i$ is affine (step 8), so $S$ is affine [lem-weil-pbc-affine-morphism-permanence] (2).

source.place: Left implicit in Stacks' proof of 01ZT ('Hence the result follows from the Noetherian case'); written out by the agent with Limits Lemma 01YW

Statement kept. Proof in nine steps following 01ZT: S qc, separated (09MQ node) and quasi-separated (written out); reduction to f of finite presentation by the existing 09YZ node (generalization of 09YY; finite = integral + lft by the existing leaf) and the 01Z6 leaf; absolute Noetherian approximation (closed node prop-nagata-noetherian-inverse-system, reindexed by the existing leaf), S_i Noetherian; descent of f to g_0 by thm-pd-spreading-out (01ZM) and the 01YZ node; g_i finite for large i (01ZO node), surjective for large i (07RR node; a step Stacks omits), X_i affine for large i (01Z6); S_i affine by the one new unsplit node lem-weil-pbc-finite-surjective-affine-target-noetherian (01YQ; no Mathlib match after leansearch, leanfinder, loogle and grep); S affine since S -> S_i is affine.
